title_en: Henan Yanshi Xinlong Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Luoyang Institute of Science and Technology and Henan No.6 Construction Engineering Company — dispute over claim and outstanding project payments
ruling_gist_en: When a construction project is halted due to an incorrect geological report provided by the employer, and the parties have not agreed or reached an agreement on the duration of the work stoppage, the contractor should not blindly wait and allow the work stoppage to continue and the losses to expand. full_text_en:
Henan Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Luoyang Institute of Science and Technology and Henan No.6 Construction Engineering Company — dispute over claims and outstanding project payments

【Ruling Summary】

Where a construction project is suspended due to an erroneous geological report provided by the employer, and the parties have neither agreed nor reached a consensus on the duration of the suspension, the contractor shall not blindly await the continuation of the suspension and the expansion of the losses caused thereby. The determination of the suspension period as the basis for calculating the losses resulting from such suspension shall not simply rely on the natural duration of the suspension state; instead, a reasonable period shall be comprehensively determined based on the facts of the case as the suspension period.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment
(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 292

Petitioner (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance, Applicant for Retrial): Henan Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at Ditou Village, Yuetan Town, Yanshi City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Liuxin, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yang, lawyer of Beijing Tianyi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yang Zilong, staff of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Respondent for Retrial): Luoyang Institute of Science and Technology, domiciled at No. 90 Wangcheng Avenue, Luolong District, Luoyang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Xiaolin, President of the Institute.

Agent ad litem: Niu Peiwei, lawyer of Henan Kaiwu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Xiaojie, Head of the Infrastructure Section of the Institute.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Respondent for Retrial): Henan Liujian Construction Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Yard No. 38 Wangcheng Road, Xigong District, Luoyang City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Chao Lu, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Yunli, Legal Counsel of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Shang Jiaquan, lawyer of Beijing Gaowen Law Firm.

Petitioner Henan Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinlong Company) filed a petition with this Court against the Civil Judgment (2006) Yu Fa Min Zai Zi No. 106 rendered by the Henan High People's Court, in the case of dispute over claims and outstanding project payments with Respondents Luoyang Institute of Science and Technology (hereinafter referred to as the Institute, formerly known as Luoyang University) and Henan Liujian Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Liujian Company, formerly known as Henan No.6 Construction Engineering Company). On December 3, 2009, this Court rendered the Civil Ruling (2009) Min Jian Zi No. 109, deciding to retry this case, and during the retrial, the enforcement of the original judgment was suspended. After the retrial was initiated, a collegial panel was formed in accordance with the law, and a hearing was conducted on October 20, 2011. Yang Liuxin, legal representative of Xinlong Company, and agents ad litem Liu Yang and Yang Zilong; agents ad litem of the Institute, Niu Peiwei and Li Xiaojie; agents ad litem of Liujian Company, Li Yunli and Shang Jiaquan, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now concluded.

On March 10, 2001, Xinlong Company filed a lawsuit with the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court of Henan Province, alleging that due to the erroneous geological report provided by the Institute and the inadequate organization, command, and coordination by Liujian Company, the project subcontracted to Xinlong Company, namely the Institute's adult education building and residential building, was suspended, causing huge economic losses to Xinlong Company. Additionally, the completed work of Xinlong Company had not been settled, and the project payments were in arrears. Therefore, Xinlong Company requested: 1. an order that Liujian Company and the Institute compensate Xinlong Company for the economic losses of RMB 3.035 million caused by their fault; 2. an order that Liujian Company and the Institute immediately pay the outstanding project payments of RMB 1,252,579.4; and 3. that the litigation costs of this case be borne by Liujian Company and the Institute.

Liujian Company argued that Xinlong Company's claim for compensation from Liujian Company was unfounded. 1. Before the quality problems in the adult education building were discovered, Xinlong Company had already breached the construction schedule. The project was due for completion on April 25, 1999, but when the suspension notice was issued on April 20, the main structure was not yet finished. 2. The substandard construction quality was caused by Xinlong Company's own fault, and the suspension was due to the substandard construction quality of Xinlong Company; thus, the losses should be borne by Xinlong Company itself. 3. After the suspension, Xinlong Company failed to actively rectify the problems, making it impossible to resume work. Regarding the issue of outstanding project payments, since the project had not been finalized or audited, it could not be determined whether there were any outstanding payments, and therefore there was no issue of payment.

The Institute argued that: 1. The subject of the construction contract for the residential building and the adult education building was the Institute and Liujian Company; Xinlong Company was not a party to the contract and had no direct interest with the Institute, so the Institute should not be a defendant in this case. 2. The rights and obligations stipulated in the subcontract between Xinlong Company and Liujian Company had no bearing on the Institute. 3. The direct cause of the cracks in the adult education building was the substandard construction quality, which led to the suspension of the project; thus, the losses from the suspension should be borne by Xinlong Company itself. 4. The discrepancy in the geological report had no direct causal relationship with quality problems such as floor slab cracks. 5. Xinlong Company's allegation that the Institute concealed the truth had no factual basis. 6. The Institute did not owe any project payments to Xinlong Company. 7. The Institute had no fault whatsoever and did not cause any losses to Xinlong Company.

The Luoyang Intermediate People's Court found at first instance: On June 18, 1998, the Institute and Liujian Company entered into a Construction Contract through a bidding process, under which the Institute contracted out the adult education building and residential building to Liujian Company. The contract stipulated the project name, location, scope, contract price, duration, quality grade, and method of contracting, among other matters. To organize the construction, Liujian Company subcontracted the above project to Xinlong Company the next day, and the two parties signed the "Luoyang University Project Subcontract," which, in addition to requiring Xinlong Company to perform the construction obligations under the contract between the Institute and Liujian Company, further clarified Xinlong Company's responsibilities. In the subcontract, Liujian Company assumed management obligations as the construction manager. Thereafter, Xinlong Company commenced construction at the Institute's construction site in the name of Liujian Company's Luoyang University Project Department. Luoyang Huacheng Construction Supervision Firm (hereinafter referred to as Huacheng Firm) served as the project's supervision unit and supervised the project.

In January 1999, after cracks were discovered in the cast-in-place slabs on the western half of the adult education building, Huacheng Firm issued a notice of rectification and suspension to the Luoyang University Project Department on January 16. On January 20, Liujian Company's Engineering Management Department issued a suspension notice to the Luoyang University Project Department, and work on the adult education building was completely halted. Regarding the crack issue in the adult education building, on January 24, 1998, Yuzhong Geological Survey Engineering Company and the Department of Civil Engineering of the Institute produced the "Luoyang University Adult Education Building and Residential Building Geotechnical Engineering Investigation Report," concluding: "The pile end bearing stratum should be placed on the fifth layer of silty clay," with a bearing capacity value of 1500 Kpa for that layer. On November 18, 1998, a letter from the Fourth Design and Research Institute of the Ministry of Machinery Industry to the Institute's Infrastructure Office stated: "The 'Luoyang University Adult Education Building Pile Foundation Inspection Report' found that the ultimate end resistance of some pile tips differs significantly from the original geological data." "If not addressed, it is likely to cause uneven foundation settlement, tilting, cracking, and other adverse consequences in the building." In January 1999, cracks were discovered in the adult education building. On June 26, 1999, the Luoyang Municipal Construction Committee convened the design, construction, supervision, and other units to analyze and discuss the causes of the cracks in the cast-in-place slabs of the adult education building, resulting in the "Minutes of the Meeting on Analysis of Causes of Cracks in Luoyang University Adult Education Building." The second point of the minutes stated: "Given that the geological survey was conducted by the Department of Civil Engineering of the Institute, which lacks the relevant qualifications, and the bearing capacity provided differs somewhat from the foundation bearing capacity reflected in the pile inspection report, the Institute is required to commission a qualified survey unit to conduct a new survey." On June 29, Yuzhong Geological Survey Engineering Company was commissioned to conduct a geological verification survey, and on July 1, the company replied, confirming that the original survey report complied with relevant regulations. In late October, the Institute commissioned Luoyang Planning and Architectural Design and Research Institute to conduct a supplementary survey. In November, that institute produced the "Luoyang University Adult Education Building and Residential Building Geotechnical Engineering Investigation Report (Supplement)," which concluded and recommended: "The standard value of ultimate end resistance of the fifth layer of silty clay at the site is qp=1300kpa; the standard value of ultimate end resistance of the sixth layer of silt and silty clay is qpk=1200kpa in the north and east, and 750-900kpa in the west and south." "For the adult education building, foundation reinforcement is required." Thereafter, the Institute commissioned the original design unit, the Fourth Design and Research Institute of the Ministry of Machinery Industry, to redesign the foundation. On March 13, 2000, that institute, based on the survey report of Luoyang Planning and Architectural Design and Research Institute, made changes to the foundation design of the adult education building. In the "Design Change Notice," the reason for the change was clearly stated: " Due to the erroneous geological report provided by the client (the Institute)." During the trial of this case at first instance, the Institute commissioned the Henan Provincial Construction Engineering Quality Inspection and Testing Center Station to inspect the quality of the adult education building. On June 25, 2001, the station issued a "Quality Inspection Report," concluding: "The cracks are not caused by uneven foundation settlement." When the report was examined during the trial, Xinlong Company denied the report on the grounds that it was biased and that it was commissioned unilaterally by the Institute during the litigation. In October 2001, the court of first instance commissioned the National Center for Quality Supervision and Testing of Construction Engineering to inspect the causes of the cracks in the adult education building. The conclusion was: "The cracks are caused by uneven foundation settlement between the two axes." During the trial at first instance, Liujian Company had already reinforced the foundation according to the revised foundation reinforcement drawing.

From the time the cracks were discovered and construction was suspended until the filing of the lawsuit, nearly two years were spent on analyzing the causes of the cracks, expert deliberations, and determining responsibility. Liujian Company and the Institute could not prove that during this period they made any arrangements regarding when Xinlong Company would resume work, whether personnel would be withdrawn, or whether machinery would be relocated, nor did they report to the relevant authorities as required by the regulation that "a construction project suspended for more than two months shall be reported to the competent department." From the suspension on April 16, 1999, until the filing of the lawsuit on March 6, 2001, a total of 691 days, the losses included: machinery and equipment standby fees of RMB 423,873.91; loss of construction turnover materials of RMB 1,533,693.42; and idle labor costs of RMB 93,030. Additionally, the project had leased a six-ton tower crane from the Sixth Branch of Luoyang Xinchang Construction and Installation Engineering Company. In accordance with the civil judgment (2001) Luo Jing Zhong Zi No. 215 of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court, Xinlong Company was ordered to pay compensation at the rate of RMB 100 per day (calculated from April 19, 1999, to January 18, 2003) totaling RMB 135,000. The total of the above was RMB 2,118,559.73.

The court of first instance further found: The inspection conclusions of the Henan Provincial Construction Engineering Quality Inspection and Testing Center Station's Quality Inspection Reports No. 92 and No. 100 of 1999 on the adult education building stated: "The concrete strength of the sampled piles within axes 6-14 on the second and fourth floors is below the strength grade." The inspection conclusion of the Henan Provincial Academy of Building Research's Inspection Report No. 026 of 1999 on the adult education building stated: "The estimated concrete strength on the first floor slab, axes 1-6; the second floor slab, axes 8-11; and the fourth floor slab, axes 6-8, and 8-1 is below C20." The above confirmed that there were some quality problems in Xinlong Company's construction.

The court of first instance also found: The Department of Civil Engineering of the Institute did not have the qualifications for engineering surveys and did not hold a business license. Regarding Xinlong Company's claim of outstanding project payments by the Institute and Liujian Company, on January 4, 2003, Xinlong Company indicated that, due to the involvement of a third party in the materials related to the electrical and plumbing parts, affecting the calculation of the work volume, it would be difficult to provide the final accounts to the court in the short term. Accordingly, Xinlong Company first withdrew the claim for payment of project payments, reserving the right to file a separate lawsuit after the final accounts were prepared.

The court of first instance held: The construction contract for the adult education building and residential building was between the Institute and Liujian Company, and the Institute was clearly the owner. In the execution of the contract, Xinlong Company carried out construction in the name of the Luoyang University Project Department. During construction, cracks appeared in the adult education building. It has now been found that the cracks were "caused by uneven foundation settlement," and the uneven foundation settlement was due to the erroneous "Luoyang University Adult Education Building and Residential Building Geotechnical Engineering Investigation Report" provided by the Institute. That investigation report was jointly produced by Yuzhong Geological Survey Engineering Company and the Department of Civil Engineering of the Institute. The Institute, lacking survey qualifications and a business license, jointly produced the geotechnical investigation report with another party, which was the main cause of the report's errors, and thus the Institute bears fault. As the owner of the adult education building, the Institute should have provided accurate and correct drawings to the construction unit. In this case, the erroneous foundation drawings provided by the Institute caused the cracks in the adult education building and the suspension of Xinlong Company's work. Therefore, the Institute shall bear primary liability for the losses resulting from the suspension. Since Xinlong Company's claim is for damages, seeking tort civil liability rather than contractual liability for breach of contract, the Institute's defense that it was not a proper defendant because it did not have a direct contractual relationship with Xinlong Company for the construction of the adult education building is untenable. Liujian Company, having failed to handle the situation properly after the cracks were discovered, thereby expanding the losses, shall bear certain responsibility. Xinlong Company had some quality problems in its construction. Although these quality problems were not the cause of the cracks in the adult education building, the quality issues in its work had a unsettling effect on the Institute, and the suspension of work was in part due to that unease. Therefore, Xinlong Company shall also bear some responsibility for the suspension. Based on the above, the court of first instance rendered Civil Judgment (2001) Luo Jing Chu Zi No. 67, ordering: (1) Liujian Company to compensate Xinlong Company for economic losses of RMB 211,855.97 within 10 days after the judgment takes effect; (2) the Institute to compensate Xinlong Company for economic losses of RMB 1,694,847.79 within 10 days after the judgment takes effect; (3) the remaining losses of RMB 211,855.97 to be borne by Xinlong Company itself. The case acceptance fee of RMB 31,447, the appraisal fee of RMB 50,000, and other costs of RMB 6,289.4, totaling RMB 87,736.4, were to be borne by Xinlong Company and Liujian Company each in the amount of RMB 8,773.64, and by the Institute in the amount of RMB 70,189.12.

Dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, the Institute filed an appeal with the Henan High People's Court, arguing: 1. The facts found in the judgment of first instance were unclear. The "subcontract" between Liujian Company and Xinlong Company constituted a total subcontract, which violated mandatory legal provisions and should be invalid. The reason for the suspension of the adult education building project was the construction quality problems of Xinlong Company, which had no necessary causal relationship with whether the geological report was erroneous. The cracks in the adult education building were caused by construction quality issues. The "failure to report to the competent authority" cannot be a reason for the Institute to bear liability. Xinlong Company's losses were not factual. Xinlong Company never submitted to Liujian Company or the relevant departments any claim for the inventory or compensation of personnel, equipment, or materials. The claim for compensation raised in the litigation had no factual basis. 2. The facts found in the judgment of first instance were erroneous. Yuzhong Geological Survey Engineering Company is a qualified company. The "Geological Investigation Report" jointly produced by that company and the Institute was considered. In October 1998, the Fourth Design and Research Institute of the Ministry of Machinery Industry made changes to the design of the adult education building based on the pile foundation inspection results. The Institute was not at fault. 3. The application of law in the judgment of first instance was erroneous. This case should be a dispute over a construction project contract, but the judgment of first instance treated it as a tort dispute as the legal basis for accepting the case. The Institute requested the court of second instance to ascertain the facts and amend the judgment accordingly.

Liujian Company appealed, arguing that the part of the judgment of first instance regarding Xinlong Company's claim for compensation was unclear in terms of facts. During the trial at first instance, Xinlong Company did not provide valid evidence for its claim, nor did it follow the contract provisions or the industry norms for construction projects regarding the claims procedure. The losses claimed for 691 days were caused by Xinlong Company itself. Liujian Company was not at fault and should not bear compensation liability.

Xinlong Company, in response to the Institute's appeal, argued: 1. Although Liujian Company subcontracted the entire project to Xinlong Company, Liujian Company dispatched several personnel in the name of the Luoyang University Project Department to be present on site for management. Therefore, the contract and performance model between Xinlong Company and Liujian Company complied with laws and regulations. Xinlong Company's entry into the site for construction was also recognized by the Institute. 2. The cause of the suspension was the erroneous geological survey report provided by the Institute. The Fourth Design and Research Institute of the Ministry of Machinery Industry twice sent letters to the Institute, pointing out that the partial pile tip resistance differed significantly from the geological data, and if left unaddressed, it could lead to adverse consequences such as uneven foundation settlement, tilting, and cracking. The Institute paid no attention and allowed Xinlong Company to continue construction, leading to cracks after the main structure was completed. 3. Xinlong Company had already filed a separate lawsuit regarding the lease of turnover materials, in which the Institute also participated. Xinlong Company's losses could be proved by documentary evidence, physical evidence, and relevant effective judgments.

Xinlong Company, in response to Liujian Company's appeal, argued: 1. After Liujian Company and the Institute ordered the suspension in April 1999, Xinlong Company's construction machinery, turnover materials, and personnel remained at the site. In January 2001, Liujian Company and Xinlong Company signed an agreement for withdrawal and payment, and Xinlong Company withdrew from the construction site of the adult education building. However, the machinery, turnover materials, and personnel remained at the site awaiting settlement. 2. When floor slab cracks were discovered in April 1999, the Institute and Liujian Company ordered a suspension. After the suspension, the cause of the cracks was being investigated and analyzed, and Xinlong Company was told to await results and be ready to resume work at any time. Until the cause of the cracks was determined, it was impossible for Xinlong Company to submit a claim. 3. Regarding the 691-day suspension, a meeting was held on August 2, 1999, to discuss resumption of work, and minutes were formed. The minutes proved that Xinlong Company was under suspension, not a withdrawal. Xinlong Company did not withdraw from the construction site until after 2001, but construction materials, turnover materials, and personnel remained at the site. Because Liujian Company failed to settle accounts with Xinlong Company, the losses were further expanded, and Liujian Company should bear compensation liability.

The Henan High People's Court found at second instance: On April 20, 1999, due to quality issues in the adult education building, Liujian Company issued a suspension notice to Xinlong Company. On April 25 of the same year, Liujian Company issued a notice to Xinlong Company for the suspension of all personnel and withdrawal from the site. The other facts found by the court of second instance were the same as those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that: 1. Regarding the validity of the "Luoyang University Project Subcontract" executed by the Sixth Construction Company and Xinlong Company. After the Sixth Construction Company contracted the Institute of Technology's adult education building, it subcontracted the entire project to Xinlong Company. Although the prime contract and the subcontract were two separate contracts with different parties, the subject matter of the contracts was connected. After subcontracting the project it had contracted, the Sixth Construction Company did not withdraw from the contractual relationship; as the party bearing overall responsibility for the construction project it had contracted, it still assumed responsibilities such as organizing construction, technical documentation, quality management, and coordinating the relationship between the construction unit and the Institute of Technology, and it dispatched multiple personnel on-site under the name of the Luoyang University Project Department to supervise the construction quality of the construction unit. In particular, after cracks appeared in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology, it actively analyzed and investigated the causes and ordered the construction unit to suspend work. Judging from the Sixth Construction Company's conduct of still being responsible for the project after subcontracting it, there was no situation where the Sixth Construction Company, for profit, subcontracted the contracted project to other construction units without assuming any technical, quality, or economic responsibility for the project. The performance model of the "Luoyang University Project Subcontract" entered into by the Sixth Construction Company and Xinlong Company did not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations. After Xinlong Company signed the project subcontract with the Sixth Construction Company, it became a party to the prime contract together with the Sixth Construction Company, jointly assuming responsibility for the contracted adult education building of the Institute of Technology. The Institute of Technology's appeal arguing that the subcontract signed between the Sixth Construction Company and Xinlong Company was in fact a sub-subcontract, which violated the prohibitive provisions of law and should be invalid, was untenable and not supported.

2. Regarding the issue of who should bear liability for the cracks in the adult education building and how the losses due to work stoppage should be calculated. The court of second instance, considering all the facts of the case, held that all three parties bore liability for the cracks in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology and the work stoppage losses, and should bear corresponding liability according to the degree of causation. According to the quality inspection reports No. 92 and No. 100 of 1999 commissioned by the Sixth Construction Company from the Henan Provincial Construction Engineering Quality Testing Center, and the testing report No. 026 of 1999 from the Henan Provincial Academy of Building Research, all the above appraisal conclusions proved that the concrete strength of the adult education building project of the Institute of Technology constructed by Xinlong Company was lower than the design strength grade, and recommended that relevant departments take measures. Under the circumstances where the quality problems of the project constructed by Xinlong Company had not been resolved and rectified, Huacheng Firm issued a work stoppage and rectification notice to Xinlong Company, requiring Xinlong Company to rectify the problems caused by non-standard construction. The above expert opinions and appraisal conclusions all proved that Xinlong Company did have quality problems during construction. The existence of such circumstances had a certain impact on the parties' inability to timely and objectively understand the cause of the cracks in the adult education building, thereby leading to work stoppage and the prolonged stay of Xinlong Company's personnel on site, causing corresponding losses. For this reason, Xinlong Company should bear a certain degree of liability for the losses caused by the idling of its own personnel and equipment. However, the true cause of the cracks in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology was the uneven settlement of the foundation caused by the erroneous geological report provided by the Institute of Technology. Before the adult education building of the Institute of Technology was completed, on November 18, 1998, the Fourth Design and Research Institute of the Ministry of Machinery Industry sent a letter to the Capital Construction Office of the Institute of Technology, pointing out that the pile end resistance of part of the adult education building of the Institute of Technology differed greatly from the geological data, and if not treated, it could likely cause adverse consequences such as uneven settlement of the building foundation, tilting, and cracking of the building. The Institute of Technology did not take measures in response. After work on the adult education building was suspended, on June 26, 1999, the Luoyang Municipal Construction Committee organized a special meeting attended by exploration, design, construction, and supervision units to analyze the cause of the building cracks and formed a summary, requiring the Institute of Technology to commission a qualified exploration unit to re-explore. On January 27, 2000, the Luoyang Municipal Construction Committee organized multiple experts to discuss the cause of the cracks, concluding that "the original engineering geological report was insufficient in depth and the conclusions were erroneous." On March 13, 2000, the Fourth Design Institute of the Ministry of Machinery Industry made design changes, with the reason for the change being "due to errors in the geological report provided by Party A." On November 16, 2001, the National Center for Quality Supervision and Testing of Construction Engineering tested the cause of the cracks in the adult education building, concluding that "...the unevenness of the bearing layer of the foundation piles and the high value of the empirical parameters for bearing capacity were possible causes of uneven foundation settlement." The above facts demonstrate that there was a direct causal relationship between the cracks in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology and the erroneous geological report provided by the Institute of Technology. If it were a construction quality issue, the geological report and design would not have been changed repeatedly. Based on expert opinions and appraisal conclusions, where the Institute of Technology could not provide conclusive evidence to prove that the cause of the cracks in its adult education building had no direct causal relationship with whether the geological report was erroneous, the court of first instance, relying on relevant expert opinions and scientific appraisal conclusions, determined that the Institute of Technology, as the owner, should provide accurate construction drawings and geological reports to the construction unit. Because the drawings and geological report it provided to the construction unit were erroneous, leading to cracks in the adult education building and causing Xinlong Company to suspend work, the Institute of Technology should bear primary liability. This determination was not improper. However, the proportion and amount of liability determined by the court of first instance against the Institute of Technology were inappropriate and should be corrected. The Sixth Construction Company, as the department responsible for quality management, supervision, and overall responsibility for the Luoyang University Project, should be accountable to the Institute of Technology above and to the construction unit below. The Sixth Construction Company was ineffective in organizing and coordinating the resolution of issues such as whether Xinlong Company should continue construction during the process of analyzing and determining the cause of the cracks after they appeared in the adult education building. Furthermore, it failed to take effective measures to avoid losses to the subcontractor after the work stoppage, causing Xinlong Company's personnel and equipment to remain idle at the construction site for a prolonged period. Therefore, the Sixth Construction Company should also bear corresponding liability for the losses caused to Xinlong Company. Regarding the basis for calculating losses. Because it was necessary to ascertain the cause of the cracks in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology after they appeared, the search and analysis of the cause continued after the work stoppage. Before the cause of the cracks was determined, the Institute of Technology and the Sixth Construction Company had not given Xinlong Company a clear position. Although the Sixth Construction Company issued work stoppage and site evacuation notices to the construction unit on April 20 and April 25, 1999, it was not clear at that time that Xinlong Company would not be allowed to continue construction, nor did the evacuation notice specify whether it was personnel evacuation or evacuation of both personnel and equipment. Under these circumstances, it was reasonable for Xinlong Company, after ceasing work, to leave personnel to watch over the site and keep machinery and turnover materials on the site in preparation for future resumption of work. Moreover, the cause of the work stoppage could not be entirely attributed to Xinlong Company. The losses from idle labor, idle machinery, and turnover of building materials resulting from the work stoppage should not be borne solely by Xinlong Company. Based on the cause of the work stoppage and the reason Xinlong Company's machinery and turnover materials could not be promptly removed, Xinlong Company, the Sixth Construction Company, and the Institute of Technology should bear liability for the losses caused by the work stoppage in proportion to their respective contributions. Given that the main cause of the cracks in the adult education building was the uneven foundation settlement due to errors in the geotechnical engineering investigation report provided by the Institute of Technology, and after the cracks appeared, the Institute of Technology neither faced its own responsibility nor gave clear instructions on whether to resume work or allow Xinlong Company to continue construction, making it difficult for Xinlong Company to promptly decide whether to stay or leave, the Institute of Technology should bear primary liability for the losses caused to Xinlong Company from idle machinery, turnover materials, and idle labor due to the work stoppage. The specific proportion of liability was determined to be 50%. The Sixth Construction Company's ineffective communication and coordination had a causal relationship with the prolonged work stoppage of Xinlong Company and its failure to timely evacuate the site, so it should also bear corresponding liability for the work stoppage and idle loss losses. The proportion of its liability was determined to be 20%, with the remaining losses borne by Xinlong Company itself. However, the period for calculating the work stoppage and idle losses determined by the court of first instance as 691 days was too long. According to Henan Provincial Department of Construction Document No. 21 (1999), "Notice on Provisions for Recording Loss Expenses Related to Suspended Projects," the period for suspension of construction is generally 3 months. If it exceeds 3 months, the parties should negotiate for slowdown or cessation of construction. In this case, when the cracks in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology made it impossible for the project to continue, none of the three parties acted in accordance with the principle of good faith and cooperation under contract law to objectively investigate the cause and take positive remedial measures. Instead, they shifted blame onto others to varying degrees and avoided their own responsibilities. However, after the work stoppage had continued for a period, Xinlong Company itself should have realized that work could not resume in the short term and should have immediately taken measures to avoid the expansion of losses. It was not entitled to claim compensation for the expanded losses. Accordingly, the period for calculating Xinlong Company's work stoppage and idle losses was determined by the court of second instance to be 6 months from April 16, 1999, when Xinlong Company ceased work. For the work stoppage situation thereafter, Xinlong Company should have taken measures to change it, so it was no longer included in the compensation period. Based on the facts found by the court of first instance, Xinlong Company's 691-day idle machinery shift fees were RMB 423,873.91, building turnover material losses were RMB 1,533,693.42, labor idle losses were RMB 93,030, and compensation paid for renting a 6-ton tower crane was RMB 135,000, totaling RMB 2,185,597.33. Xinlong Company's 6-month work stoppage loss would be RMB 534,162.6 (idle machinery shift fees, building turnover material losses, and labor idle losses: RMB 2,050,597.33 divided by 691 days = daily loss of RMB 2,967.57 multiplied by 6 months); compensation paid for renting a 6-ton tower crane was RMB 135,000, at RMB 100 per day for a total of 6 months, totaling RMB 18,000. The sum of these two parts was RMB 552,162.6. The Institute of Technology compensated Xinlong Company for 50% of the loss, i.e., RMB 276,081.3. The Sixth Construction Company bore 20% of the compensation liability, i.e., RMB 110,432.52. The remaining losses were borne by Xinlong Company. The court of first instance failed to consider that Xinlong Company should have taken necessary measures to prevent the expansion of losses during the period when the cause of the cracks in the adult education building was being investigated, and the basis for determining Xinlong Company's 691-day loss was insufficient and should be corrected. Other fees collected by the court of first instance were without basis and should not be collected. In summary, the facts found in the judgment of first instance were basically clear, but the outcome was inappropriate and should be modified. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Henan High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2003) Yu Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 140: (1) Setting aside the Civil Judgment (2001) Luo Jing Chu Zi No. 67 of the Luoyang Intermediate People's Court; (2) The Institute of Technology shall compensate Xinlong Company for economic losses of RMB 276,081.3 within 10 days after the judgment becomes effective; (3) The Sixth Construction Company shall compensate Xinlong Company for economic losses of RMB 110,432.52 within 10 days after the judgment becomes effective; (4) Dismissing Xinlong Company's other claims. Court acceptance fee for first instance of RMB 31,447 and appraisal fee of RMB 50,000, totaling RMB 81,447, were borne by the Institute of Technology in the amount of RMB 40,723.5, by the Sixth Construction Company in the amount of RMB 16,289.4, and by Xinlong Company in the amount of RMB 15,723.5. Court acceptance fee for second instance of RMB 31,447 was borne by the Institute of Technology in the amount of RMB 15,723.5, by the Sixth Construction Company in the amount of RMB 6,289.4, and by Xinlong Company in the amount of RMB 9,434.1.

Xinlong Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of second instance, applied for retrial to the Henan High People's Court, arguing: 1. The Fourth Design and Research Institute of the Ministry of Machinery Industry had already sent a letter to the Institute of Technology on November 18, 1998, pointing out that the pile foundation test report of the adult education building of the Institute of Technology was erroneous. The Institute of Technology should bear primary liability for the work stoppage losses. 2. The Henan Provincial Department of Construction Document No. 21 (1999) did not apply to this case, and the work stoppage period should not be calculated as six months. The court of first instance correctly calculated the work stoppage time. 3. Xinlong Company had no initiative regarding testing, commencement of work, or site evacuation, could not foresee the duration of the work stoppage, and repeatedly requested a proper resolution to the work stoppage issue. It had no fault in the expansion of losses. It requested the revocation of the judgment of second instance and the maintenance of the judgment of first instance.

The Institute of Technology argued in its defense: 1. The party directly liable for the work stoppage losses was Xinlong Company. Appraisals showed that the cracks were caused by unqualified construction materials used by Xinlong Company. After multiple appraisals, the pile foundation and geological data were unrelated to the cracks. 2. Xinlong Company maliciously expanded the losses. On May 22 and 27, 1999, the Institute of Technology notified the project department to evacuate the site, but Xinlong Company refused and continued construction on the residential building. Xinlong Company never made a request regarding the losses and took no measures. 3. The judgment of second instance correctly calculated the loss over six months and should be affirmed.

The Sixth Construction Company argued in its defense: 1. After the judgment of second instance was issued, Xinlong Company has not applied for enforcement against the Sixth Construction Company to date, which should be deemed as a waiver of rights. 2. Regarding work stoppage losses, the state stipulates three months. The judgment of second instance, calculating over six months, already fully protected Xinlong Company's rights and interests and was correct. It requested affirmation.

The facts retried by the Henan High People's Court were the same as those found by the court of second instance.

The Henan High People's Court held at the retrial: After Xinlong Company discovered cracks in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology during the construction process, the three parties conducted multiple investigations, inspections, appraisals, and expert discussions on the cause of the cracks in the adult education building. In particular, during the first instance, the court of first instance again commissioned the National Center for Quality Supervision and Testing of Construction Engineering to test the cause of the cracks. The above circumstances demonstrated that the Institute of Technology, as the owner, should have provided accurate construction drawings and geological reports to the construction unit. Because the drawings and geological report it provided to the construction unit were erroneous, leading to cracks in the adult education building and causing Xinlong Company to suspend work, the judgments of first and second instance correctly determined that the Institute of Technology bore primary liability. The concrete strength of the adult education building project of the Institute of Technology constructed by Xinlong Company was lower than the design strength grade. When Huacheng Firm conducted quality self-inspection of the project constructed by Xinlong Company, it also found multiple quality problems in the ongoing project. Without resolving or rectifying these multiple quality problems, it issued a work stoppage and rectification notice to Xinlong Company, requiring Xinlong Company to rectify the problems caused by non-standard construction. Expert opinions and appraisal conclusions all proved that Xinlong Company did have quality problems during construction. The existence of such circumstances had a certain impact on the parties' inability to timely and objectively understand the cause of the cracks in the adult education building, thereby leading to work stoppage and the prolonged stay of Xinlong Company's personnel on site, causing corresponding losses. Accordingly, the judgment of second instance, ordering the Institute of Technology to bear 50% liability and Xinlong Company to bear a certain degree of liability for the losses caused by the idling of its own personnel and equipment, was not improper. In this case, after the event causing work stoppage occurred, the parties Xinlong Company, the Institute of Technology, and the Sixth Construction Company did not actively negotiate a resolution but instead blamed and shifted responsibility onto each other, leading to further expansion of the work stoppage losses. In particular, Xinlong Company, as the actual construction party, should have taken necessary measures to prevent the expansion of losses after the work stoppage had continued for a period but failed to do so. Regarding Xinlong Company's work stoppage losses, the judgment of second instance, with reference to the relevant provisions of Henan Provincial Department of Construction Document No. 21 (1999), "Notice on Provisions for Recording Loss Expenses Related to Suspended Projects," discretionarily determined a period of 6 months. This did not violate legal provisions and was also correct. In summary, the judgment of second instance had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and a proper outcome, and should be affirmed. Xinlong Company's retrial application grounds were untenable and were dismissed. Pursuant to Article 184 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Henan High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2006) Yu Fa Min Zai Zi No. 106: Affirming the Civil Judgment (2003) Yu Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 140.

Xinlong Company, still dissatisfied, appealed to this Court, requesting the revocation of the judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment, and a new judgment according to law. The reasons were: 1. Henan Provincial Department of Construction Document No. 21 (1999), "Notice on Provisions for Recording Loss Expenses Related to Suspended Projects," is not a law, administrative regulation, or departmental rule. The judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment erroneously relied on this document to determine the work stoppage period as 6 months. 2. The content of the above document cannot cover the circumstances of this case. The judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment using this document as the basis for determining the work stoppage period constituted an error in the application of law. 3. In this case, Xinlong Company could not foresee the duration of the work stoppage, nor was there an issue of neglecting to take measures resulting in the expansion of losses. The judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment erroneously found that Xinlong Company failed to take necessary measures resulting in the expansion of losses. 4. The allocation of liability for work stoppage losses and the determination of the amount of losses in the judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment were clearly unfair.

The Institute of Technology argued in its defense that the judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment were correct in both fact-finding and application of law, and Xinlong Company's appeal should be dismissed. 1. The application of law in the judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment was correct. The reference to Henan Provincial Department of Construction Document No. 21 (1999), "Notice on Provisions for Recording Loss Expenses Related to Suspended Projects," in determining Xinlong Company's work stoppage period as 6 months was an exercise of the discretionary power of the courts of second instance and retrial in finding the fact of Xinlong Company's work stoppage period and did not violate legal provisions. 2. The determination of the work stoppage period as 6 months in the judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment was correct. The Sixth Construction Company issued work stoppage and site evacuation notices to Xinlong Company on April 20, 1999, and May 25, 1999, but Xinlong Company refused to evacuate. Furthermore, Xinlong Company failed to take necessary measures thereafter, resulting in the expansion of work stoppage losses, and should bear liability for the expanded losses. 3. The work stoppage losses determined in the judgment of first instance were too high. The determination of the work stoppage period as 6 months in the judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment, and calculating work stoppage losses accordingly, was appropriate.

The Sixth Construction Company argued in its defense that Xinlong Company's appeal grounds were untenable and its request should be dismissed. 1. The Sixth Construction Company had no fault regarding the work stoppage, and moreover, Xinlong Company refused to evacuate the site after receiving the work stoppage and site evacuation notice from the Sixth Construction Company. Therefore, the Sixth Construction Company should not bear any compensation liability for Xinlong Company's losses. 2. Under these circumstances, the Sixth Construction Company, for the sake of settling the matter, waived its appeal and accepted the judgment of second instance and the retrial judgment. On April 11, 2008, it settled with Xinlong Company regarding multiple judgments and mediation documents involving their economic dealings, including the judgment of second instance in this case, during the enforcement process, and reached an "Enforcement Settlement Agreement." On April 15, 2008, the Sixth Construction Company paid Xinlong Company RMB 269,000 in accordance with the settlement agreement, and all economic disputes between the parties were fully settled. Therefore, the Sixth Construction Company should no longer bear any liability for Xinlong Company's work stoppage losses in this case.

Facts Found by the Court

It was found at trial that on May 25, 1999, Henan No. 6 Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "No. 6 Construction") held a quality meeting for the Luoyang University adult education building project. According to the meeting minutes, Wu Zhihao, manager of No. 6 Construction, demanded of Yang Liuxin, manager of Xinlong Company: "All personnel shall withdraw. Find reliable personnel to seal off all sites, especially the adult education building; no one is permitted to enter." Yang Liuxin responded, "It can be done." On the same day, No. 6 Construction issued a notice to Xinlong Company directing all personnel to stop work and withdraw. Cao Guanzhou signed and received the notice on May 27, 1999. With respect to Cao Guanzhou's identity, Xinlong Company acknowledged that he was a staff member of No. 6 Construction assigned to the Luoyang University project department.

On August 2, 1999, No. 6 Construction held a meeting on the resumption of work for the Luoyang University adult education building and residential building. According to the meeting summary, No. 6 Construction required the "subcontractor," i.e., Xinlong Company, to resume work in mid-August with a construction period of 100 days. Cai Baoxiang, deputy manager of No. 6 Construction, also demanded that "the construction period must be guaranteed... If any further incident occurs involving Yang Liuxin, the company will adopt a tough stance." Yang Liuxin stated, "We will certainly complete the work with guaranteed quality and quantity as required by the company, and arrange for personnel to enter the site as soon as possible." However, as reflected in letters from Xinlong Company to the Institute of Technology and No. 6 Construction dated October 26, 1999, and March 4, 2000, as well as the statements of all parties in the first instance, second instance, and retrial proceedings, the project did not resume work in mid-August 1999, and the parties had still not reached an agreement on suspension or resumption due to the cracking issue in the adult education building.

On January 20 and January 21, 2001, Xinlong Company and No. 6 Construction signed two "Agreements," stipulating that "(No. 6 Construction) Company shall pay Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. RMB 500,000 in project funds on January 22, 2000" and "before February 7, while the Institute of Technology and Provincial No. 6 Construction Company perform their obligations regarding the funds, the construction site of the adult education building shall be vacated for Provincial No. 6 Construction Company." Subsequently, because neither party performed the agreements, No. 6 Construction filed a lawsuit with the Xigong District People's Court of Luoyang, Henan Province, and a mediation was reached under the auspices of that court. The Xigong District People's Court rendered Civil Mediation Document No. (2001) Xi Jing Chu Zi No. 175 on March 20, 2001, clearly stating that "the defendant (i.e., Xinlong Company) shall withdraw from the site." The above evidence is recorded in Volume 2 and Volume 3 of the main case file of (2001) Luo Jing Chu Zi No. 67.

During the court trial, No. 6 Construction submitted the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" signed with Xinlong Company on April 11, 2008, the "Enforcement Record" of April 14, and the receipt for payment of April 15, to prove that all debts and credits between itself and Xinlong Company, including those relating to the dispute in this case, had been fully settled. On April 11, 2008, the "Enforcement Settlement Agreement" signed between No. 6 Construction and Xinlong Company stipulated: "1. The party subject to enforcement (i.e., No. 6 Construction) shall pay the applicant (i.e., Xinlong Company) RMB 269,000 within five days after signing. The payment shall be made to the applicant before April 18, 2008; otherwise, enforcement shall proceed according to the original judgment. 2. All economic transactions, project payments, and disputes over leased equipment between the two parties are fully settled." On April 14, 2008, in the "Enforcement Record" prepared by the Intermediate People's Court of Luoyang, Henan Province, Huang Yuqun, the agent of No. 6 Construction, stated: "Our leadership agrees... The amount in Civil Judgment No. (2003) Yu Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 140 is RMB 126,721.92... After offsetting, we will concede another RMB 50,000, so we actually pay RMB 269,000 and bear the enforcement fee of RMB 8,700." Yang Liuxin, the agent of Xinlong Company, stated: "Our position is that after full offset of the principal amount, we will concede another RMB 50,000, actually receiving RMB 269,000. The payment must be credited to our company's account or paid in cash before April 18. The enforcement fee of RMB 8,700 shall be borne by the other party." Both agents signed the "Enforcement Record." On April 15, 2008, Yang Liuxin issued a receipt to No. 6 Construction stating: "Received today from Provincial No. 6 Construction Company RMB Two Hundred Sixty-Nine Thousand Yuan (RMB 269,000) as court enforcement payment." Xinlong Company acknowledged the above evidence and facts, and this Court confirms them.

Other case facts found by this Court are the same as those found by the courts of first instance, second instance, and retrial.

Additionally, during the trial before this Court, Xinlong Company abandoned the application reason stated in its retrial petition that this case is a tort dispute, and that the second instance judgment and retrial judgment erred in applying contract law by finding that Xinlong Company should bear responsibility for its own expanded losses. At the same time, it further clarified its claim for retrial, asserting that for its losses due to suspension of work, the Institute of Technology should bear 70%, No. 6 Construction should bear 20%, and it should bear 10% itself.

Opinion of the Court

This Court is of the opinion that, synthesizing the claims, defenses, and main arguments of all parties during the trial before this Court, the focus of the dispute in this case is how the Institute of Technology and No. 6 Construction should bear the losses due to work suspension claimed by Xinlong Company. This specifically involves two issues: first, the duration of the work suspension; second, the proportion of apportionment of the losses from work suspension.

Regarding the duration of work suspension. In this case, after cracks were discovered in the floor slabs of the adult education building, on April 16, 1999, Huacheng Firm issued a notice to the Luoyang University project department to suspend work for rectification; on April 20, the Engineering Management Department of No. 6 Construction issued a work suspension notice to the Luoyang University project department, deciding that "work on the Luoyang University adult education building shall be suspended from today." At that point, all work on the adult education building was suspended. To ascertain the cause of the cracks in the adult education building, after the work suspension, both the Institute of Technology and No. 6 Construction repeatedly commissioned different third-party organizations to conduct appraisals of the adult education building project. Due to differences in conclusions, for nearly two years from the date of suspension to the filing of the first instance case on March 19, 2001, the parties were unable to reach a consensus on the cause of the cracks. During this period, on May 25, 1999, No. 6 Construction held a quality meeting for the Luoyang University adult education building project. According to the meeting minutes, Wu Zhihao, manager of No. 6 Construction, demanded that Xinlong Company withdraw, and Yang Liuxin, manager of Xinlong Company, agreed. On the same day, No. 6 Construction issued a written notice of work suspension and withdrawal, requiring Xinlong Company to "stop work and withdraw all personnel." The notice was signed and received on May 27 by Cao Guanzhou, a staff member of No. 6 Construction assigned to the Luoyang University project department. However, this notice was also not actually implemented. On August 2, 1999, No. 6 Construction held a meeting on the resumption of work for the Luoyang University adult education building and residential building. According to the meeting summary, No. 6 Construction required the "subcontractor," i.e., Xinlong Company, to resume work in mid-August with a construction period of 100 days. Cai Baoxiang, deputy manager of No. 6 Construction, also demanded that "the construction period must be guaranteed... If any further incident occurs involving Yang Liuxin, the company will adopt a tough stance." Yang Liuxin stated, "We will certainly complete the work with guaranteed quality and quantity as required by the company, and arrange for personnel to enter the site as soon as possible." However, as reflected in letters from Xinlong Company to the Institute of Technology and No. 6 Construction dated October 26, 1999, and March 4, 2000, as well as the statements of all parties in the first instance, second instance, and retrial proceedings, the project did not resume work in mid-August 1999, and the parties had still not reached an agreement on suspension or resumption due to the cracking issue in the adult education building. It was not until January 20 and January 21, 2001, that Xinlong Company and No. 6 Construction signed two "Agreements," stipulating that "(No. 6 Construction) Company shall pay Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. RMB 500,000 in project funds on January 22, 2000" and "before February 7, while the Institute of Technology and Provincial No. 6 Construction Company perform their obligations regarding the funds, the construction site of the adult education building shall be vacated for Provincial No. 6 Construction Company." However, both parties still failed to perform the agreement. No. 6 Construction then filed a lawsuit with the Xigong District People's Court of Luoyang, Henan Province, and a mediation was reached under the auspices of that court. The Xigong District People's Court rendered Civil Mediation Document No. (2001) Xi Jing Chu Zi No. 175 on March 20, 2001, clearly stating that "the defendant (i.e., Xinlong Company) shall withdraw from the site."

From the above facts, it can be seen that after the suspension of work on the adult education building on April 20, 1999, there was ongoing dispute between Xinlong Company and No. 6 Construction over whether to suspend work and withdraw or to resume work. In this regard, the parties should have negotiated and resolved the matter in accordance with the principle of good faith. If it was temporarily difficult to reach an agreement, the party awarding the contract should have given clear instructions on work suspension and withdrawal, and should bear reasonable losses from the suspension; the contractor and subcontractor should not have blindly waited, allowing the losses from suspension to expand, but should have taken appropriate measures, such as promptly informing the relevant parties of the work suspension and properly withdrawing personnel and machinery, to reduce their own losses. In this case, after the suspension of work on the adult education building, the Institute of Technology, as the party awarding the contract, did not give clear instructions on work suspension, withdrawal, or whether to resume work. No. 6 Construction was ineffective in organizing and coordinating the resolution of issues such as whether Xinlong Company would continue the construction, and did not take effective measures to avoid Xinlong Company's losses from work suspension. The Institute of Technology and No. 6 Construction should bear certain responsibility for this. At the same time, Xinlong Company also did not actively take appropriate measures to require the Institute of Technology and No. 6 Construction to clarify the duration of the work suspension or whether all personnel and machinery needed to be withdrawn. Instead, it blindly waited for nearly two years, thereby allowing the losses from work suspension to expand. Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, although the adult education building project was actually in a state of suspension for nearly two years, the duration of work suspension for calculating losses should be reasonably determined in light of the overall case facts. The second instance judgment and the retrial judgment, synthesizing the degree of responsibility of each party and with reference to the provisions of the "Notice on Provisions for Recording Related Loss Expenses for Work Suspension" (Yu Jian Biao Ding (1999) No. 21) issued by the Henan Provincial Department of Construction, calculated Xinlong Company's work suspension period as six months starting from April 20, 1999. This is relatively reasonable. Xinlong Company's argument that applying this notice to determine the work suspension period as six months constitutes an error in the application of law is not well-founded. The second instance judgment and the retrial judgment accordingly found that for the subsequent work suspension and idling, Xinlong Company should have taken measures to change the situation, and such period should not be included in the scope of compensable losses. This is not improper. Xinlong Company shall bear responsibility itself for the losses caused by its failure to take appropriate measures. Xinlong Company's argument that it was not negligent in taking measures to prevent the expansion of losses is also not well-founded.

Regarding the amount of losses from work suspension. Based on the above determination of the calculation period for Xinlong Company's losses from work suspension, this Court finds that Xinlong Company's losses from six months of work suspension amount to RMB 534,162.6 (machine and equipment stand-by costs, losses from building turnover materials, and labor idling losses: RMB 2,050,597.33 divided by 691 days = daily loss of RMB 2,967.57 multiplied by 6 months); compensation paid for the rental of a six-ton tower crane: RMB 135,000, at RMB 100 per day for a total of 6 months, totaling RMB 18,000. The above two parts sum to RMB 552,162.6.

Regarding the proportion of apportionment of losses from work suspension. With respect to the responsibility for the work suspension caused by cracks in the adult education building of the Institute of Technology, the first instance, second instance, and retrial judgments, based on the case facts found at trial, determined that the Institute of Technology provided an erroneous geological report, which led to the cracks in the adult education building and caused Xinlong Company's work suspension, and therefore should bear primary responsibility; No. 6 Construction was ineffective in handling the matter, resulting in the expansion of losses, and Xinlong Company's project quality had certain defects, so both should bear some responsibility. Xinlong Company has no objection to these facts and findings, and the Institute of Technology and No. 6 Construction have also not filed a petition for retrial against the second instance and retrial judgments. This Court confirms this. The first instance judgment accordingly determined that the Institute of Technology should bear 80% of the losses, and No. 6 Construction and Xinlong Company should each bear 10% of the losses. This constitutes a division of responsibility proportions within the normal scope of discretion and is not clearly improper. The second instance and retrial judgments, while finding the first instance's determination of responsibility correct, adjusted the Institute of Technology's primary responsibility from 80% to 50%. This is inconsistent with their own relevant conclusions and lacks sufficient evidence, and should be corrected. Furthermore, during the trial before this Court upon petition for retrial, Xinlong Company claimed that for the losses from work suspension, the Institute of Technology should bear 70%, No. 6 Construction should bear 20%, and it should bear 10% itself. Xinlong Company's claim has factual and legal basis and should be supported. Therefore, the Institute of Technology shall bear 70% of the losses, No. 6 Construction shall still bear 20% of the loss liability as determined by the second instance and retrial judgments, and Xinlong Company shall bear 10% itself.

As No. 6 Construction and Xinlong Company had already reached an enforcement settlement during the enforcement proceedings in April 2008 (after the retrial judgment of the Henan Provincial High People's Court became effective and before this Court's trial upon petition) regarding the relevant creditor-debt disputes between them, including the economic losses to be borne by No. 6 Construction to Xinlong Company involved in this case, and the settlement has been fully performed, and since the obligations to be borne by No. 6 Construction under this judgment (including the bearing of litigation costs) have not changed, their creditor-debt relationship concerning this case has been fully settled.

In summary, pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Civil Judgment No. (2006) Yu Fa Min Zai Zi No. 106 of the Henan Provincial High People's Court is vacated;

2. Items 1, 3, and 4 of Civil Judgment No. (2003) Yu Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 140 of the Henan Provincial High People's Court are affirmed;

3. Item 2 of Civil Judgment No. (2003) Yu Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 140 of the Henan Provincial High People's Court is vacated;

4. Luoyang Institute of Technology shall compensate Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. for economic losses in the amount of RMB 386,513.82.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 31,447; appraisal fee: RMB 50,000; total: RMB 81,447. Luoyang Institute of Technology shall bear RMB 57,012.9; Henan No. 6 Construction Group Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 16,289.4; Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 8,144.7. Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 31,447. Luoyang Institute of Technology shall bear RMB 22,012.9; Henan No. 6 Construction Group Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 6,289.4; Yanshi Xinlong Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 3,144.7.

This judgment is final.
